newsitem.title: USA: LanChile wants slow US air pact liberalization.
newsitem.headline: LanChile wants slow US air pact liberalization.

text.p: Chile and the United States should liberalize their aviation agreements, but do so slowly, a top Chilean airline offical told Reuters this week.

"We cannot have immediately open skies, but we have to accept more frequencies," said Ignacio Cueto, president of the Lan Cargo Group, in an interview on Tuesday. Cueto and several investors control LanChile and all-cargo FastAir, both based in Santiago.
"It must be step-by-step," he said. "The Chilean airlines are not 100 percent ready for open skies now."

He said that when flight restrictions are lifted and the big U.S. carriers begin bloody competition, it is the Latin American airlines, which are smaller, that are most harmed by the battle. "When (AMR Corp's ) American and (UAL Corp's ) United start a fight between them, it puts us in a very difficult position," he said.

No open skies talks are currently scheduled, but Chile and the United States are currently negotiating to liberalize the combination regime which expired November 30, according to U.S. Department of Transportation Spokesman Bill Mosley. "We expect talks soon," Mosley said.
